own_solution.law: The rod speed is v = sqrt(Y/rho), its fundamental frequency is f = v/(2L), and adjacent dust heaps are separated by d = c/(2f) = cL sqrt(rho/Y). Using Y = 7.0e10 Pa gives v = 5091.75 m/s, f = 2121.56 Hz and d = 8.08366 cm. Adding 32 cm to the rod gives d = 10.2393 cm.
assumptions: The uniform thin rod obeys linear elasticity.
The light disc negligibly loads the rod.
The added rod segment forms a continuous uniform rod, clamped at its resulting midpoint.
Dust heaps mark adjacent displacement nodes.

T94AF.regime: Thin-rod longitudinal approximation; all listed diameters satisfy the supplied criterion 10d < Lr.

T9574.regime: Thin-rod longitudinal approximation; all listed diameters satisfy the supplied criterion 10d < Lr.

defect_reasons.other: The authors' rationales for T2604 and TFBD6 falsely describe metal welded onto a railing, whereas the rendered sentences extend the hanging wire; these claims misidentify the physical object and operation.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with the governing relations, including rod extensions of 14, 32 and 55 cm. The actual wire extensions are disconnected from the target, so the erroneous railing rationales do not change the correct D assignments. The explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve 32 cm. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag because pass 2 identifies TFBD6 and TFE55 as deliberate numeral-free controls rather than claimed numerical minimal pairs. I refine the diameter assignments from C to K: diameter cancels in the one-dimensional rod equations, while applicability of those equations requires a slender rod. All listed diameters comfortably satisfy that regime. Cross-sectional area cancels between axial rigidity and mass per unit length. The base problem and individual rendered problems are physically well-posed; the invalid verdict concerns the authors' false wiring descriptions.
